tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear Path for Target Disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a disk that is not on top, relocate every smaller disk that lies above it to other pegs, ensuring the target disk becomes the topmost disk on its source peg.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a disk that is buried under smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: If disk 4 is under disk 2 on a peg, first move disk 2 elsewhere before moving disk 4.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Build Goal Stack in Decreasing Size
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Construct the final tower on the goal peg by placing disks from the largest down to the smallest, never placing a larger disk on top of a smaller one.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When assembling the final configuration on the target peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: First move disk 5 onto the empty goal peg, then disk 4, then disk 3, and so on.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive Phase Planning (Move‑k‑Disks)
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Solve the sub‑problem of moving k disks by recursively moving the top k‑1 disks to an auxiliary peg, moving the k‑th disk to the target, then moving the k‑1 disks onto it.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to transfer a stack of several disks between pegs.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To move three disks from peg A to peg C, first move two disks to peg B, move the third to C, then move the two from B to C.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Do Not Prematurely Place Small Disks on Goal
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Never move a small disk onto the goal peg before all larger disks that must sit below it have already been placed correctly.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During construction of the final stack, especially when the goal peg already contains some disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Do not place disk 1 on the goal peg before disk 5, 4, 3 are already there.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Legal Move Invariant
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Every move must satisfy two conditions: the source disk is the topmost disk on its peg, and the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 3 onto a peg whose top disk is 2 is illegal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat Existing Goal Disks as Fixed Base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Once a disk is correctly placed on the goal peg and all larger disks beneath it are also correctly placed, treat that disk as an immovable base for the remaining moves.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After a disk has been positioned in its final location on the goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: After placing disk 5 at the bottom of the goal peg, never move it again.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Exploit the Smallest Disk’s Flexibility
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be placed on any peg without violating size constraints, making it ideal for temporarily clearing paths and enabling larger moves.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need a free peg or to unblock a larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Move disk 1 to a spare peg to free disk 2 for a move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Post‑Construction Verification
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After generating the full move list, replay the moves from the initial configuration to confirm that each move is legal and that the final configuration matches the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: At the end of your solution generation, before outputting the move list.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Simulate the sequence step‑by‑step and check the final peg states.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recognize Classic Single‑Peg Configuration
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Detect when all disks start stacked on a single peg and the goal is the same ordered stack on another peg; in this case, the standard recursive solution can be applied directly.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: If the initial configuration has every disk on one peg and the goal peg is empty.
tower-of-hanoi.example: All disks on peg 0, goal is peg 2 – use the classic Hanoi algorithm.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Generate Moves Recursively with Explicit Disk IDs
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Implement the recursive Hanoi algorithm by explicitly naming the disk being moved in each step, ensuring the output format includes the disk identifier.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When constructing the move list programmatically.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Append [3, source, target] when moving disk 3.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Violating size rule: moving a larger disk onto a smaller one.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may forget the rule that larger disks cannot be placed on top of smaller disks, especially when focusing on moving a target disk.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always check the top disk of the destination peg; only move a disk if the destination is empty or its top disk is larger.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a non‑top disk without clearing the path.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may try to move a buried disk without first relocating the smaller disks above it.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Apply the Clear Path for Target Disk principle: first move all smaller disks above the target.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Final configuration does not match the goal state.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may lose track of the overall objective or miss a final verification step.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Perform Post‑Construction Verification by replaying the moves and comparing the final state to the goal.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Incorrect peg indexing (off‑by‑one or swapped pegs).
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: Confusion between 0‑based indexing used in the answer format and natural 1‑based peg labeling.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Consistently use 0‑based indices throughout and double‑check each move's from and to values.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Premature placement of small disks on the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may place a small disk on the goal peg before larger disks that belong below it have been positioned.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Follow the Do Not Prematurely Place Small Disks on Goal principle; only place a small disk on the goal after all larger required disks are already there.
